newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi sees tough talks over Italy welfare reform.
newsitem.headline: Prodi sees tough talks over Italy welfare reform.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday that coming talks with centre-left coalition allies and trade unions over welfare reform would be "hard and tough".
"... there is agreement on opening the negotiations, the contents have to be defined, it will be a hard and tough discussion," he told reporters after the cabinet approved a corrective mini-budget.

Prodi repeated that the negotiations on welfare reform would start in mid-April and promised that any deal would be enshrined in the 1998 budget, which has to be approved by parliament by the end of the year.

"I am calling on all the responsible powers in the country, businesses, unions, government and opposition because Italy will have a great future if it can face up to and resolve these problems," Prodi said.

He said the mini-budget, which aims to raise 15.5 trillion lire ($9.2 billion) in 1997 and cut the budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic, could lead to renewed dialogue with the opposition.

"The package was approved unanimously, I think the reading of it could lead to a recovery in dialogue with the opposition. There are no elements for a brawl," Prodi said. -- Rome newsroom +39 6 678 2501
